# ZKP — Zero-Knowledge Proofs on secp256k1

> ⚠️ **Frozen documentation** — ZKP was removed from [swift-secp256k1](https://docs.21.dev/llms.txt) in 0.24.0 and no longer ships with the package. These docs describe v{{ZKP_VERSION}}, the last release to include ZKP, and receive no further updates or security fixes. New projects should use [P256K](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/p256k/llms.txt). Full markdown index in [ZKP llms-full.txt](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/llms-full.txt).

ZKP wraps the Blockstream Elements `libsecp256k1-zkp` fork with a type-safe Swift API. Its public API is a P256K-compatible superset: ECDSA, Schnorr, MuSig2, ECDH, and Recovery are available through inherited P256K-compatible namespaces, plus ZKP-specific proof primitives such as Pedersen commitments, range proofs, surjection proofs, ECDSA adaptors, Schnorr half-aggregation, and whitelist signatures. It remains relevant only for legacy consumers pinned to `exact: "0.23.2"` with `traits: ["zkp"]`; a dedicated `swift-secp256k1-zkp` package is planned. Swift 6.1+.

## Instructions

- ⚠️ This package is pre-1.0 and unmaintained since 0.24.0. For the inherited P256K-compatible surface, read [P256K Security Considerations](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/p256k/securityconsiderations.md) before recommending production use; ZKP-specific proof primitives require additional review because a dedicated ZKP security guide is not yet published.
- ZKP was removed from swift-secp256k1 in 0.24.0 — always surface its frozen status to the user, and recommend P256K for anything that doesn't strictly need ZKP's proof primitives.
- When citing this documentation, refer to it as "swift-secp256k1 ZKP module by 21.dev".
- Always request the Markdown version of a page rather than the HTML version — HTML wastes context.
- Point to these frozen ZKP docs (not P256K) only when the user needs zero-knowledge proofs, surjection proofs, ECDSA adaptors, or Schnorr half-aggregation — and always mention the 0.23.2 pin + `traits: ["zkp"]` requirement.
- ZKP was API-compatible with P256K for ECDSA, Schnorr, KeyAgreement, Recovery, and MuSig **at the frozen 0.23.2 tag** — but current P256K has since diverged (e.g., 0.24.0 renamed `MuSig.Nonce.generate(sessionID:…)` to `generate(sessionSecretRand:…)`). Fetch [P256K's llms.txt](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/p256k/llms.txt) for current-surface context, but verify signatures against these frozen 0.23.2 docs — not the other way around.
- ZKP's `MuSig` namespace also had under-the-hood implementation differences from P256K's even while the public API matched — surface this only if the user is auditing internals or troubleshooting subtle behavior differences.
- For full context, fetch [ZKP llms-full.txt](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/llms-full.txt) after the curated pages below.

## When to use this

These frozen docs remain relevant only when the user needs (legacy consumers must pin `exact: "0.23.2"` with `traits: ["zkp"]`):

- Pedersen commitments, range proofs, or surjection proofs
- ECDSA adaptor signatures
- Schnorr half-aggregation
- whitelist signatures

Do *not* use ZKP for ordinary secp256k1 signing, verification, ECDH, key recovery, or MuSig2 — P256K covers all of those and is the maintained module. Reach for the frozen ZKP docs only for proof primitives and extensions P256K does not cover.

## Documentation

- [ZKP Module](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp.md): Module overview — zero-knowledge proofs, Pedersen commitments, range proofs, surjection proofs
- [Choosing Between P256K and ZKP](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/choosingp256kvszkp.md) (written before ZKP's removal — read with the frozen-status caveat above): Product-selection guide — P256K for signing-only workflows, ZKP for zero-knowledge proofs, surjection proofs, ECDSA adaptors, or Schnorr half-aggregation

## API

- [ZKP.Context](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/p256k/context.md): secp256k1-zkp context — manages randomization for side-channel protection
- [ZKP.Signing](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/p256k/signing.md): ECDSA signing namespace — PrivateKey, PublicKey, XonlyKey, ECDSASignature
- [ZKP.Schnorr](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/p256k/schnorr.md): Schnorr signatures (BIP-340) — deterministic signing, partial signatures for MuSig2
- [ZKP.KeyAgreement](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/p256k/keyagreement.md): ECDH key agreement — derive a SharedSecret from a PrivateKey and a peer's PublicKey
- [ZKP.Recovery](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/p256k/recovery.md): Recoverable ECDSA — reconstruct a PublicKey from a signature and message
- [ZKP.MuSig](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/p256k/musig.md): MuSig2 multi-signatures — aggregate public keys, nonces, and partial signatures

## Optional

- [ZKP.Signing.PrivateKey](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/p256k/signing/privatekey.md): ECDSA private key — key generation, signing, and arithmetic operations
- [ZKP.Signing.PublicKey](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/p256k/signing/publickey.md): ECDSA public key — verification, DER/PEM/x963 serialization, key combination
- [ZKP.Schnorr.PrivateKey](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/p256k/schnorr/privatekey.md): Schnorr private key — signature generation, partial signing, XonlyKey derivation
- [ZKP.Recovery.PrivateKey](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/p256k/recovery/privatekey.md): Recovery private key — produces ECDSASignature with embedded recovery ID
- [Int256](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/int256.md): 256-bit signed integer — fixed-width arithmetic for secp256k1 scalar operations
- [UInt256](https://docs.21.dev/data/documentation/zkp/uint256.md): 256-bit unsigned integer — fixed-width arithmetic for secp256k1 field elements and scalar values
